provenance: Hand-labeled at the vulnerability level from resources in the vendored terragoat/cfngoat trees, described in tool-neutral language and deliberately independent of any scanner's rule grain (no Checkov/tool rule IDs). High-consensus IaC misconfigurations only, spread across AWS/Azure/GCP. Intended as the fair cross-tool comparison set for SEC-39.

items.notes: S3 bucket is publicly readable (public-read ACL, no public-access protections). The scanner emits several rows for this bucket; collapsed to the 2 genuine human-level vulns - this item is the public exposure (see GT-002 for the encryption vuln).

Same bucket as GT-001, second distinct vulnerability: no server-side encryption at rest for a data bucket. Deliberately separated from the public-access vuln - a human names these as two different problems.

Security group allows inbound SSH (port 22) from 0.0.0.0/0. Collapsed away a separate rule-description hygiene row that is not a real security vuln; the genuine issue is management-port exposure to the internet.

IAM policy grants wildcard actions/resources (over-permissive). The scanner emits ~6 rows (credentials exposure, unconstrained write, data exfiltration, privilege escalation, etc.); collapsed to the single underlying vulnerability - a policy using '*' rather than least privilege.

A long-lived AWS access key is hard-coded into the EC2 user-data script. The scanner reports this as both a generic secret and a user-data-secret row; collapsed to one hard-coded-credential vulnerability.
NSG inbound rules allow SSH (22) and RDP (3389) from any source ('*'). Collapsed the two rules into one 'management ports open to the internet' vulnerability.
Managed disk has encryption explicitly disabled (encryption_settings.enabled = false) - unencrypted storage of data at rest. Single distinct vulnerability.
Database administrator password is hard-coded as a string literal in the Terraform. Single distinct vulnerability (hard-coded credential in IaC).

Managed MySQL server has public network access enabled - the database is reachable from the public internet. High-consensus public-exposure of a data store (sibling of public-storage); collapsed any related rows to this one exposure vuln.
GCS bucket grants objectViewer to 'allUsers' - the bucket contents are world-readable. Single distinct public-exposure vulnerability.
Firewall allows ingress from 0.0.0.0/0 to all TCP ports (0-65535). Collapsed the scanner's multiple rows to one 'network open to the internet' vulnerability.
Cloud SQL instance has a public IPv4 and an authorized network of 0.0.0.0/0 - the database is exposed to the entire internet. High-consensus public-exposure; collapsed related rows to this one vuln.
